d.a: Distribution: — Vietnam: provinces Lam Dong and Khanh Hoa (Khanh Le Pass area in Bidoup Nui Ba National Park). The species is likely to be endemic to a very restricted area of Hon Giao Ridge at elevations of 1700 – 1900 m a. s. l. Conservation status: — Aspidistra brachypetala var. danii was observed in a single locality where it is occasionally common in understory of a primary forest in an area of less than 1 km 2. This area is legally protected, being located within the territory of Bidoup Nui Ba National Park. If the forest does not degrade due to recreation or any other factors, the conservation status of this variety is to be assessed as Near Threatened (NT) following the formal criteria of IUCN (2025). Notes: — Aspidistra brachypetala var. danii differs from the type variety of A. brachypetala C. R. Lin & B. Pan in Pan et al. (2020: 195), which is endemic to Guangxi (China), in spherical to slightly oblate (rarely broadly ellipsoidal) perianth tube with ± flat base (vs. broadly ellipsoidal or ovoid perianth tube with broadly conoid base), dimorphic perianth lobes arranged in two distinct whorls (vs. subequal lobes arranged seemingly in one whorl), and broadly triangular outer tepal lobes with bases narrower than maximum width, showing auricle-like lobules (vs. outer tepal lobes triangular, widest at base and thus lacking any lobules). The finding studied here represents a significant extension of the known distribution range of A. brachypetala, being a new species record for Vietnam, and distanced about 1080 km to the south from its only previously documented locality. Within the classification of shapes of perianth tubes by Tillich (2023), the tube of A. brachypetala var. danii is to be described as urceolate due to its flat base, whereas the tube of A. brachypetala var. brachypetala (although described as urceolate in the protologue) corresponds to the ellipsoidal type. To avoid confusion, we here appeal to the geometrical shape rather than to the tube classification.
